rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a referent the room cannot resolve stalls the slide. Present: chunk 2 "Three ways agents break the old story": line 17: "You can't fully predict the combination, only bound it." The combination of what is never named; the long-read sentence that named it (instructions, context and the user's ask combined) was cut in the re-chunk, so the antecedent is stranded. Closest passes: line 9 "the old story" resolves to chunk 1's header; line 25 "the agent-risk lens" and "the reports" are definite nouns first met here (see suggestions).
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name what combines: what the instructions, context and tools add up to.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 9 "the old story" points at chunk 1 of the same file by claim, not at another file by position. grep for opening lecture/earlier lecture/prework in body: none.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 3 "You built something that works." The referent is the student's own build from earlier modules, the module-arc beat the rule-1 carve-out names; no "the X you did/saw" pointing at a missing beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest: line 11 "Same prompt, same files, same tools, different session, different answer." It is a verbless stack, but it follows the verbed claim "The behaviour is non-deterministic." and enumerates conditions, not a live demo scene or terminal guess-cue; the muted read loses nothing. No guess-before-reveal beat in the body.
Closest: chunk 0 line 3 "Testing, policy and certification do not give agent systems certainty." carries a standalone claim; every ## chunk holds its own claim.

Closest: line 9 "Three ways agents break the old story" over three claims (non-deterministic, instruction-set attack, emergent) plus the figure; line 21 "Assess, then mitigate" over Assess. and Mitigate. Headers are true summaries.

Closest: line 19 "What may the agent read? What may it change? What must come back to a human?" is an anaphora triple whose third leg carries new content (the human gate); line 11 "Same prompt, same files, same tools" third leg new (tools). No Not-X-Not-Y-Z, no self-grading superlative, no number+retraction, no empty verb leg in body. Line 37 "Damn, this is complex stuff." is mood-contract attested at maintainer L112.

suggestions.now: The agent-risk lens asks what the agent can reach, leak, and be misled into by ordinary text. Read the reports with judgment.
